values.Background: The Trans-Arabian Pipeline (Tapline) was a crude oil pipeline running from Qaisumah in Saudi Arabia across Jordan, southern Syria (including the Golan Heights), and into Lebanon, terminating at the Sidon (Zahrani) Mediterranean export terminal. Constructed 1947-1950 by the Trans-Arabian Pipeline Company (a subsidiary of Aramco) using 30-inch and 31-inch steel pipe over a 1,213-1,214 km route, with six main pumping stations (Nariya, Qaisumah, Rafha, Badanah, Turaif in Saudi Arabia; Qaryatain in Jordan). Initial capacity 320,000 bpd, expanded via auxiliary pumping in 1957 to ~450,000 bpd and a peak nameplate of ~500,000 bpd. The cross-border line ceased operating in 1976 as the Lebanese Civil War began and supertankers eroded its economics; the Saudi and Jordanian portions continued intermittently until 1983/1990. Final 'de-cruding' (cleaning of residual crude) was completed in 2001. Designated Saudi Arabia's first industrial heritage site in December 2020.

researcher_notes: Background is a composite narrative; its constituent facts (route Qaisumah->Sidon via Jordan/Syria/Lebanon, 1947-1950 construction, 30/31-in pipe, ~1,213 km, pumping stations, 320k->500k bpd capacity, cessation 1976/1990, de-cruding 2001, heritage-site designation) are spread across the cited sources. Existing Aramco URL is dead (timeout). Britannica/Saudipedia each cover most facts but the original deterministic check failed only because it matched the whole paragraph verbatim; substantively all four kept sources support the narrative. Added encyclopedia.com (covers capacity 320k/500k, Abqaiq supply, route, Aramco). NOTE divergence: Saudipedia gives total length 1,648 km and Britannica/EC give ~1,720 km total Al-Dammam-to-Sidon vs the 754 mi (1,213-1,214 km) Qaisumah-mainline figure used by GEM -- the 'Background' correctly distinguishes the mainline figure. Heritage-site (Dec 2020) and exact 1957 auxiliary-pumping detail are sourced from Aramco/gem narrative and not independently re-verified here (Aramco dead); flagged as the weakest sub-claims.

ProposalYear=1947 ties to the start of design/construction in 1947. Both existing refs are live but do NOT state 1947 (AUB finding aid is a collection catalog; encyclopedia.com gives only WWII/postwar context) -> DEAD_LINK. Replaced with 2 independent sources that state 1947: Wikipedia ('Construction of the Trans-Arabian Pipeline began in 1947') and aleqt Arabic ('في عام 1947، بدأ تصميم ثم إنشاء خط التابلاين' = in 1947, design then construction of the Tapline began). Note: sources frame 1947 as the design/construction-start year; if GEM intends 'Proposal' strictly as agreement/concession year this is a close proxy but worth a glance.

ConstructionYear=1948 is hard to corroborate at 2+ sources. The existing Aramco URL is dead (timeout); the AUB finding aid does not state a construction year. Only one independent source explicitly gives 1948: aleqt Arabic ('في عام 1948' for physical construction start, distinguishing it from the 1947 design year). CONFLICT/nuance: Wikipedia and Britannica state construction 'began in 1947' (managed by Bechtel), so the dominant English sources put the construction start a year earlier than GEM's 1948. Could not reach 2 independent sources for the literal value 1948 -> medium (single verified source), and flagged as a likely 1947-vs-1948 ambiguity (1947 = design/award + initial works; 1948 = main physical construction) for Update review.

StartYear1=1950 (oil first flowed / pipeline inaugurated) confirmed by 4 independent sources: Wikipedia ('active during 1950-1976'), encyclopedia.com ('began operations in 1950'), Saudipedia ('inaugurated in 1950'), aleqt Arabic ('انتهت أعمال إنشاء الأنبوب الرئيس ومرافق الضخ في عام 1950'). High confidence.

StopYear=1976 marks when the FULL cross-border line ceased operating (Lebanese Civil War). Only Wikipedia explicitly anchors 1976 ('The full length of the pipeline was active during 1950-1976'). The two other existing refs are live but do NOT state 1976: AUB finding aid (catalog, no year) and encyclopedia.com (gives 'early 1980s' and '1990', not 1976) -> DEAD_LINK on those two. CONFLICT: other sources emphasize different stop years -- encyclopedia.com 'largely ceased functioning in the early 1980s'/'completely stopped operating in 1990'; Saudipedia/Aramco 'decommissioned in 1990'; aleqt 'توقف بعدها الخط تماما في أوائل التسعينيات' (~1990s). 1976 = cross-border shutdown, 1983/1990 = full decommissioning; GEM's StopYear=1976 reflects the cross-border line. Reached only 1 verified source for the literal 1976 value -> medium; flagged the 1976-vs-1990 distinction for Update.

Capacity=500,000 bpd (peak) confirmed by 3 independent sources: Wikipedia ('maximum capacity of about 500,000 bbl/d'), encyclopedia.com ('Tapline's capacity in 2003 was 500,000 barrels per day'), aleqt Arabic ('ارتفعت في وقت لاحق إلى 500 ألف برميل في اليوم' = later rose to 500,000 bpd). High. NOTE: Britannica states an erroneous 'initial capacity of 3 million barrels per day' (clear typo for 300,000) and was therefore NOT used for this unit. Initial capacity was ~300,000-320,000 bpd across sources; GEM uses the peak 500,000.

LengthKnown=1,214 km (the mainline section) confirmed by 3 independent sources: Wikipedia ('1,214 kilometres (754 mi) long'), encyclopedia.com ('754 miles (1,213 km) of the pipeline'), Britannica ('754 miles (1,213 km)'). High. NOTE divergence on TOTAL system length: Britannica/EC give ~1,069 mi (1,720 km) Al-Dammam-to-Sidon including the gathering section, and Saudipedia gives 1,648 km -- GEM's 1,214 km correctly uses the 754-mi mainline (Qaisumah-to-Sidon) figure, consistent across all three kept refs.

Diameter=30 and 31 inches confirmed by 2 independent sources: Britannica ('30-inch (760-mm) and 31-inch (790-mm) pipe') and Wikipedia ('diameter of 30 inches (760 mm) and 31 inches'). Kept Britannica (live + value present), dropped the dead Aramco URL (timeout), added Wikipedia as the 2nd independent corroboration -> DEAD_LINK (replacement done). CONFLICT noted but not used: aleqt Arabic gives '30 و32 بوصة' (30 and 32 inch), which disagrees with the 31-inch figure; the two English encyclopedic sources agree on 30/31, so GEM's value stands.

FuelSource=Abqaiq, Saudi Arabia (oil fields feeding the line) confirmed by 3 independent sources: encyclopedia.com ('carry crude oil from Abqaiq, Saudi Arabia'), Wikipedia ('supplied from the oil fields near Abqaiq'), aleqt Arabic ('خطوط الأنابيب القادمة من بقيق' = pipelines coming from Abqaiq). High.

StartLocation=Qaisumah, Saudi Arabia confirmed by 3 independent sources: Wikipedia ('oil pipeline from Qaisumah in Saudi Arabia'), encyclopedia.com ('315-mile portion from Al-Dammam to Al-Qaysumah' -- Qaisumah is the start of the 754-mi mainline that GEM tracks), aleqt Arabic ('القيصومة'). High. Qaisumah is the junction where the gathering lines from Abqaiq/Al-Dammam meet the mainline; consistent across sources.

EndLocation=Sidon Terminal (Zahrani), Lebanon confirmed by 3 independent sources: Wikipedia ('to Sidon in Lebanon'), Britannica ('to Sidon, Lebanon, on the Mediterranean Sea'), encyclopedia.com ('its western terminus a few miles south of Sidon, Lebanon'). High. The Zahrani terminal sits just south of Sidon, matching the GEM 'Sidon Terminal' value.

Owner has NO [ref] column -- these citations go to ResearcherNotes, not a [ref] cell. Ownership (Trans-Arabian Pipeline Co., a wholly owned subsidiary of Aramco; now Saudi Aramco / Saudi Arabian Oil Co.) confirmed by 3 independent sources: Wikipedia ('built and operated by the Trans-Arabian Pipeline Company ... now a fully owned subsidiary of Aramco'), Britannica ('built by a subsidiary of the Arabian American Oil Company (Aramco)'), encyclopedia.com ('constructed by the Arabian American Oil Company (ARAMCO)'). High. Historical nuance for ResearcherNotes: Tapline was originally a JV of the four Aramco partners (Standard Oil of NJ/CA, Texaco, Socony-Vacuum) before becoming a fully owned Aramco subsidiary; today succeeded by Saudi Aramco -- consistent with the GEM Owner/Parent values.
